mappings.note: The table asks not only for emotional changes but for their effect on behaviour and ways to grow positively, which is the learning turned into everyday practice. Not LO-67, because the student is not sorting the changes into categories but deciding what to do about them.
What Ramesh can do about his pimples: care of the skin in daily life. The hormonal cause is background; the advice is what earns the marks, so not LO-69.
Choosing the balanced food group over junk food for a growing adolescent is nutrition applied to daily life.

Word-jumble item whose key line is saying no to alcohol and drugs because they are addictive: a health choice in daily life. Not LO-80, because no myth or prejudice is being challenged, only a habit refused.

Corrects the claim that adolescence is only physical by requiring the changes to be sorted into physical, emotional and mental. Not LO-65, because the item is about the categories rather than about spotting a change.
Frames a question that challenges the false claim that a harmful substance can be given up at will: objectivity and freedom from a comfortable prejudice. Not LO-77, since no practice is recommended.
Lists the behavioural changes that go with mood swings, wanting independence, stronger feelings, more time with friends: recognising the observable signs of this stage.

Menstrual hygiene and safe disposal of pads is the good-sanitation-practices strand of LO-78, and the scene is about waste left near the bin. Not LO-77, because the answer is sanitation for everyone, not a personal health tip.

Two similar neck bulges with different causes, iodine deficiency in one case and normal larynx growth in the other, so the phenomenon must be traced to the right cause. The strongest cause-and-effect item in the batch.
Sorts the physical changes into boys only, girls only and common to both: a three-column classification.
Designing a poster of healthy-lifestyle tips is creativity in planning and presenting with available resources. Not LO-77, because the making of the poster, not the advice alone, is the task.
Why a seedling or newborn cannot reproduce at once: growth to reproductive maturity explained as a process.
Names the sequence of life stages from infancy to old age, which is placing a lifetime into ordered categories.
The ten-to-nineteen age band for adolescence: recognising the stage by its defining marker.
What marks the move from childhood into adolescence, namely visible physical, emotional and behavioural change rather than height alone.
The thin moustache and changed voice that Devyani notices in Venkatesh: changes spotted by observation.
Devyani's growth spurt as noticed by Venkatesh, the companion observation item.
Names adolescence as the stage between childhood and adulthood.

The point is that differences in timing and extent are normal and no one should be judged or worried by them, which is the freedom-from-fear-and-prejudice strand. Not LO-65, because no change is being identified.
The growth spurt in height as the most prominent visible change of adolescence.
Broader shoulders and wider chest in boys: an observable change named for one sex, with no comparison drawn, so LO-65 rather than LO-66.
Breast development in girls, the companion single-sex observation item.
The deepening voice is traced to the growing voice box: effect tied to cause, not merely observed.
Names the Adam's apple, the visible bump the enlarged larynx makes. Identification, while the item on why the voice deepens is on LO-69.
Sets the marked deepening in boys against the slight change in girls, an explicit differentiation between the sexes.
Facial, chest and back hair in boys: further observable changes recalled.
Acne traced to oil glands working harder and clogging pores: the cause behind a visible change.
Names secondary sexual characteristics as the category of traits that appear at puberty without being reproductive organs. A category defined, so LO-67.
Puberty named as the process by which the body becomes capable of reproduction. Process, not observable feature, so LO-70.
The start of the menstrual cycle as the internal sign of reproductive maturity: part of the same maturation process.
The twenty-eight to thirty day cycle length describes how the process runs. Not LO-72, since nothing is measured or calculated by the student.
Names menstruation as the bleeding phase of the cycle, a stage within the process.
Why myths and taboos about menstruation must be challenged: they cause fear and shame. Squarely the freedom-from-fear-and-prejudice outcome, not LO-78, which is about hygiene practice.
Menopause at forty-five to fifty-five as the end of the reproductive process.

Understanding stronger emotions so behaviour can be managed and better choices made: the learning applied to daily conduct. Not LO-69, because the item asks why the knowledge is useful, not what causes the emotions.
Why adolescents need a nutritious diet during rapid growth: nutrition applied to everyday eating.
Calcium and protein from milk, curd and paneer for bone growth: a food-to-nutrient link for daily diet.
Iron from spinach, beans, raisins and figs for blood formation, the same diet-planning outcome.
Dorothy Hodgkin and her Nobel for the structure of vitamin B12 is a story of scientific discovery. Not LO-77, since no dietary advice is being given.
Personal hygiene, bathing and keeping sweat-prone areas clean to avoid infection, is the good-sanitation-practices strand rather than the diet items on LO-77.
